--- title: "5 · Validation" --- ::: {.cell} ::: ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ```r source("R/pipeline.R") ``` ## Python ```python import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import numpy as np import pandas as pd from dgxe import * wx = pd.read_csv("data/narrabri_weather.csv") traj = pd.read_csv("data/narrabri_biomass.csv.gz") drv = make_drivers(wx) Theta = make_library(drv) tr = make_trajectories(traj, drv) ``` ::: ## Solution With a library that depends on the drivers only, the fitted equation is solved numerically, here by accumulating the predicted daily growth (the simplest ODE solver, a forward step of one day): ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ```r ## coef: intercept and term coefficients; Theta_y: day x term (one season). simulate <- function(coef, Theta_y, y0) { rate <- cbind(1, Theta_y[-nrow(Theta_y), ]) %*% coef y0 + c(0, cumsum(rate)) } ``` ## Python ```python # coef: intercept and term coefficients; Theta_s: day x term (one season). def simulate(coef, Theta_s, y0): rate = coef[0] + Theta_s[:-1] @ coef[1:] return y0 + np.concatenate([[0], np.cumsum(rate)]) ``` ::: ## Leave-one-season-out cross-validation For every genotype and every season, the model is fitted to the other 30 seasons of that genotype and used to predict the left-out season from its drivers, starting from the mean initial biomass of the training seasons. ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ```r ## Each season is predicted by a model fitted to the other seasons of the same ## genotype, starting from the mean initial biomass of those seasons. ## Returns P[genotype, season, day]. cross_validate <- function(Theta, tr, fit, genotypes = tr$genotypes) { P <- array(NA_real_, dim(tr$Y)) for (g in match(genotypes, tr$genotypes)) { d <- make_design(Theta, tr, tr$genotypes[g]) for (v in seq_along(tr$years)) { train <- d$season != v coef <- fit(d$X[train, ], d$dy[train]) P[g, v, ] <- simulate(coef, Theta[v, , ], mean(tr$Y[g, -v, 1])) } } P } ## RMSE over whole trajectories, on a fixed day (array index; 99 is day 113 ## after sowing) and at maturity. Genotypes that were not predicted are ignored. evaluate <- function(P, tr, fixed_day = 99) { err <- P - tr$Y err[, , 1] <- NA # the initial value is given last <- cbind(as.vector(row(tr$nend)), as.vector(col(tr$nend)), as.vector(tr$nend) + 1) rmse <- function(e) sqrt(mean(e^2, na.rm = TRUE)) c(trajectory_rmse = rmse(err), fixed_day_rmse = rmse(err[, , fixed_day]), maturity_rmse = rmse(err[last])) } ``` ## Python ```python # Each season is predicted by a model fitted to the other seasons of the same # genotype, starting from the mean initial biomass of those seasons. # Returns P[genotype, season, day]. def cross_validate(Theta, tr, fit, genotypes=None): P = np.full(tr.Y.shape, np.nan) for g in (tr.genotypes if genotypes is None else genotypes): i = list(tr.genotypes).index(g) d = make_design(Theta, tr, g) for s in range(len(tr.years)): train = d.season != s coef = fit(d.X[train], d.dy[train]) y0 = np.delete(tr.Y[i, :, 0], s).mean() P[i, s] = simulate(coef, Theta.array[s], y0) return P # RMSE over whole trajectories, on a fixed day (days after sowing) and at # maturity. Genotypes that were not predicted are ignored. def evaluate(P, tr, fixed_day=113): err = P - tr.Y err[:, :, 0] = np.nan # the initial value is given g, s = np.indices(tr.nend.shape) def rmse(e): return np.sqrt(np.nanmean(e ** 2)) return {"trajectory_rmse": rmse(err), "fixed_day_rmse": rmse(err[:, :, fixed_day - tr.das0]), "maturity_rmse": rmse(err[g, s, tr.nend])} ``` ::: The sparse model (STLSQ) for all 199 genotypes, with the root-mean-square error (RMSE, t/ha) over whole trajectories, on day 113 after sowing, and at maturity: ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} P <- cached("cv_stlsq.rds", cross_validate(Theta, tr, fit_stlsq)) round(evaluate(P, tr), 3) ``` ::: ## Python ```python P = cross_validate(Theta, tr, fit_stlsq) print({k: round(float(v), 3) for k, v in evaluate(P, tr).items()}) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` trajectory_rmse fixed_day_rmse maturity_rmse 0.526 0.701 0.761 ``` ::: ::: ## Predicted trajectories Season 1998, predicted by models that were fitted without it. All genotypes are shown in grey; the genotypes with the lowest, median and highest final biomass are in colour. ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} v <- match(1998, tr$years) three <- spread_genotypes(tr) cells <- which(!is.na(tr$Y[, v, ]), arr.ind = TRUE) # genotype, day long <- data.frame(genotype = tr$genotypes[cells[, 1]], das = cells[, 2] + tr$das0 - 1) d <- rbind(cbind(long, source = "APSIM", biomass = tr$Y[, v, ][cells]), cbind(long, source = "Model", biomass = P[, v, ][cells])) ggplot(d, aes(das, biomass, group = genotype)) + geom_line(colour = "#D1D5DB", linewidth = 0.2) + geom_line(data = d[d$genotype %in% three, ], aes(colour = genotype), linewidth = 0.7) + facet_wrap(~source) + scale_colour_dgxe("burgundy", "cyan", "blue") + labs(x = "days after sowing", y = "biomass (t/ha)") + theme_dgxe() + legend_top() ``` ::: ## Python ```python s = list(tr.years).index(1998) three = spread_genotypes(tr) days = np.arange(tr.Y.shape[2]) + tr.das0 alive = ~np.isnan(tr.Y[:, s]) # days before maturity fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, sharey=True, figsize=(8, 3)) for ax, title, Y in zip(axes, ["APSIM", "Model"], [tr.Y, P]): Ys = np.where(alive, Y[:, s], np.nan) ax.plot(days, Ys.T, color=GREY, lw=0.2) for g, colour in zip(three, [BURGUNDY, CYAN, BLUE]): ax.plot(days, Ys[np.searchsorted(tr.genotypes, g)], color=colour, lw=0.9, label=g) ax.set_title(title, loc="left") axes[0].legend(frameon=False) axes[0].set_ylabel("biomass (t/ha)") fig.supxlabel("days after sowing") fig.tight_layout() ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](05-validate_files/figure-html/05-2-run-1.png){width=1036.8} ::: ::: Predicted against APSIM biomass on day 113, all genotype-season pairs: ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} d <- data.frame(obs = as.vector(tr$Y[, , 99]), pred = as.vector(P[, , 99])) rmse <- sqrt(mean((d$obs - d$pred)^2)) ggplot(d, aes(obs, pred)) + geom_abline(colour = dgxe[["grey"]], linewidth = 0.4) + geom_point(colour = dgxe[["blue"]], size = 0.5, alpha = 0.2) + annotate("text", x = min(d$obs), y = max(d$pred), hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 3.4, label = sprintf("RMSE %.2f t/ha", rmse)) + coord_equal() + labs(x = "APSIM biomass (t/ha)", y = "predicted biomass (t/ha)") + theme_dgxe() ``` ::: ## Python ```python obs = tr.Y[:, :, 113 - tr.das0].ravel() pred = P[:, :, 113 - tr.das0].ravel() rmse = np.sqrt(np.mean((obs - pred) ** 2)) fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(4, 4)) ax.plot([obs.min(), obs.max()], [obs.min(), obs.max()], color="#9CA3AF", lw=0.8) ax.scatter(obs, pred, s=2, alpha=0.2, color=BLUE) ax.text(obs.min(), pred.max(), f"RMSE {rmse:.2f} t/ha", va="top") ax.set_aspect("equal") ax.set_xlabel("APSIM biomass (t/ha)") ax.set_ylabel("predicted biomass (t/ha)") fig.tight_layout() ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](05-validate_files/figure-html/05-3-run-1.png){width=604.8} ::: ::: ## Baseline without weather As a reference, each trajectory is predicted by the mean curve of the same genotype in the other seasons. This prediction does not use the weather. ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ```r ## Baseline without weather: each trajectory is the mean curve of the same ## genotype in the other seasons (held at its last value once all other ## seasons have ended), with the true initial value. lookup_trajectory <- function(tr) { hold_last <- function(v) replace(v, is.nan(v), tail(v[!is.nan(v)], 1)) P <- array(NA_real_, dim(tr$Y)) for (y in seq_along(tr$years)) { m <- apply(tr$Y[, -y, , drop = FALSE], c(1, 3), mean, na.rm = TRUE) P[, y, ] <- t(apply(m, 1, hold_last)) P[, y, 1] <- tr$Y[, y, 1] } P } ``` ## Python ```python # Baseline without weather: each trajectory is the mean curve of the same # genotype in the other seasons (held at its last value once all other # seasons have ended), with the true initial value. def lookup_trajectory(tr): seen = ~np.isnan(tr.Y) total, count = np.nansum(tr.Y, axis=1), seen.sum(axis=1) # genotype x day n = count[:, None, :] - seen # other seasons with np.errstate(invalid="ignore", divide="ignore"): P = (total[:, None, :] - np.nan_to_num(tr.Y)) / n last = (n > 0).sum(axis=2, keepdims=True) - 1 # last day seen P = np.where(n > 0, P, np.take_along_axis(P, last, axis=2)) P[:, :, 0] = tr.Y[:, :, 0] return P ``` ::: ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} base <- lookup_trajectory(tr) round(evaluate(base, tr), 3) ``` ::: ## Python ```python base = lookup_trajectory(tr) print({k: round(float(v), 3) for k, v in evaluate(base, tr).items()}) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` trajectory_rmse fixed_day_rmse maturity_rmse 0.739 0.840 1.423 ``` ::: ::: The error as a function of time: ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} days <- 2:dim(tr$Y)[3] + tr$das0 - 1 d <- rbind(data.frame(das = days, rmse = rmse_by_day(P, tr), model = "model"), data.frame(das = days, rmse = rmse_by_day(base, tr), model = "baseline")) ggplot(d[d$das <= 155, ], aes(das, rmse, colour = model)) + geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) + scale_colour_dgxe("burgundy", "blue") + annotate("text", x = 40, y = 0.5, label = "model", colour = dgxe[["blue"]], size = 3.4, hjust = 0) + annotate("text", x = 40, y = 0.2, label = "baseline", colour = dgxe[["burgundy"]], size = 3.4, hjust = 0) + labs(x = "days after sowing", y = "held-out RMSE (t/ha)") + theme_dgxe() ``` ::: ## Python ```python days = np.arange(1, tr.Y.shape[2]) + tr.das0 fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 3)) ax.plot(days, rmse_by_day(P, tr), color=BLUE, label="model") ax.plot(days, rmse_by_day(base, tr), color=BURGUNDY, label="baseline") ax.set_xlim(right=155) ax.set_xlabel("days after sowing") ax.set_ylabel("held-out RMSE (t/ha)") ax.legend(frameon=False) fig.tight_layout() ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](05-validate_files/figure-html/05-5-run-1.png){width=1036.8} ::: ::: ## Individual trajectories Held-out prediction of the sparse model (STLSQ, fitted to the other seasons) and of the baseline for one genotype and season. Forty genotypes are available. ```{ojs} //| echo: false d3 = window.d3 // local copies, see js/ Plot = window.Plot traj = FileAttachment("data/interactive/trajectories.json").json() viewof genotype = select("Genotype", traj.genotypes, "g114") viewof season = slider("Season", traj.years, traj.years.indexOf(1998)) ``` ```{ojs} //| echo: false { const g = traj.genotypes.indexOf(genotype); const line = key => traj[key][g][season].map((y, i) => ({das: traj.das0 + i, y})); const [observed, model, baseline] = ["observed", "model", "baseline"].map(line); const rmse = a => Math.sqrt(d3.mean(a.slice(1), (d, i) => (d.y - observed[i + 1].y) ** 2)); const plot = Plot.plot({ width: 640, height: 320, marginLeft: 50, x: {label: "days after sowing"}, y: {domain: [0, 18], label: "biomass (t/ha)"}, marks: [ Plot.line(observed, {x: "das", y: "y", stroke: "#9CA3AF", strokeWidth: 4}), Plot.line(baseline, {x: "das", y: "y", stroke: "#8B1E3F", strokeDasharray: "4 3"}), Plot.line(model, {x: "das", y: "y", stroke: "#014E81", strokeWidth: 2}) ] }); return html`${plot}

Grey: APSIM. Blue: model (RMSE ${rmse(model).toFixed(2)} t/ha). Dashed: baseline (RMSE ${rmse(baseline).toFixed(2)} t/ha).

`; } ``` The figure uses results computed beforehand ([`scripts/precompute_interactive.R`](https://github.com/corne00/dynamic-gxe-workshop/blob/main/scripts/precompute_interactive.R)). ## Comparison of fitting methods All methods of step 4 are evaluated in the same way: ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} scores <- cached("cv_methods.rds", t(sapply(fit_methods, function(fit) { evaluate(cross_validate(Theta, tr, fit), tr) }))) round(rbind(scores, baseline = evaluate(base, tr)), 3) ``` ::: ## Python ```python scores = pd.DataFrame({name: evaluate(cross_validate(Theta, tr, fit), tr) for name, fit in fit_methods.items()}).T scores.loc["baseline"] = evaluate(base, tr) print(scores.round(3)) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` trajectory_rmse fixed_day_rmse maturity_rmse OLS 0.519 0.687 0.758 ridge 0.523 0.702 0.749 lasso 0.528 0.712 0.750 elastic net 0.527 0.710 0.747 best subset (k = 8) 0.529 0.715 0.752 backward (k = 8) 0.529 0.713 0.754 STLSQ 0.526 0.701 0.761 baseline 0.739 0.840 1.423 ``` ::: ::: The methods are close to each other. The sparse models use fewer terms for a similar error, and all of them improve on the baseline, mainly late in the season. ## Number of terms With 12 terms there is little to remove. For a larger library that includes products of drivers (`pairs = TRUE`, 36 terms), the held-out error of backward elimination (every fifth genotype) as a function of the number of terms is: ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} Theta2 <- make_library(drv, pairs = TRUE) genotypes <- tr$genotypes[seq(1, 199, by = 5)] ks <- c(4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 20, 28, 36) by_k <- cached("rmse_vs_k.rds", data.frame(k = ks, rmse = sapply(ks, function(k) { fit <- function(X, dy) fit_subset(X, dy, k, "backward") evaluate(cross_validate(Theta2, tr, fit, genotypes), tr)[[1]] }))) ``` ::: ## Python ```python Theta2 = make_library(drv, pairs=True) genotypes = tr.genotypes[::5] ks = [4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 20, 28, 36] def rmse_for(k): def fit(X, dy): return fit_subset(X, dy, k, "backward") return evaluate(cross_validate(Theta2, tr, fit, genotypes), tr)["trajectory_rmse"] by_k = pd.DataFrame({"k": ks, "rmse": [rmse_for(k) for k in ks]}) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(by_k, aes(k, rmse)) + geom_line(colour = dgxe[["blue"]], linewidth = 0.8) + geom_point(colour = dgxe[["blue"]], size = 2) + labs(x = "number of terms (36-term library)", y = "held-out trajectory RMSE (t/ha)") + theme_dgxe() ``` ::: ## Python ```python fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 2.8)) ax.plot(by_k["k"], by_k["rmse"], "o-", color=BLUE) ax.set_xlabel("number of terms (36-term library)") ax.set_ylabel("held-out trajectory RMSE (t/ha)") fig.tight_layout() ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](05-validate_files/figure-html/05-8-run-1.png){width=720} ::: :::
